label: paragraph_title
text: ANOTHER "TIGER.

label: paragraph_title
text: N E W

label: text
text: Angry Growls And Never a Tree To Climb.

label: text
text: Following the stories of the presence in the New Territories of a wholly mythical monster, come reports of a tiger which a party comprising Europeans set out this week to shoot.

label: text
text: The story is being gleefully told in club circles of the all-night vigil of the party. The action of one bold spirit who squatted on a heap of stones armed with a rifle and with two kids as bait has come in for a great deal of amused praise, for there was no tree convenient to clamber up into safety and the tiger is said to have prowled about growling to himself all through the night.

label: text
text: The party were acting on information supplied by the villagers who have from time to time reported animals mailed and tracks found pointing pretty conclusively to the presence of a tiger in the neighbourhood. Although the mid-night sportsmen have nothing to show for the trouble taken in organising the expedition and running the risk, they are firmly convinced that there is a tiger in the neighbourhood to be had for the shooting.

label: text
text: There would appear to be a good deal of haziness in the minds of those who remember seeing the tiger which was actually shot in the New Territories as to what happened to it. Several statements were made most definitely to a "China Mail" representative this morning by people who should have known. "It's in the museum here" was one. "It was skinned and made into a rug and was either given to Sir Henry May, who was Governor at the time, or is in the museum," said another. "The skin was taken off badly and had to be thrown away," was a third version.

label: text
text: There is nothing improbable in their story of its presence there, for those residents who were in the Colony a few years ago will remember the body of the tiger shot by Mr. D. Burlingham in the New Territories being carried in the streets. A cast of the impression of another tiger's "pugs" was also exhibited in the window of Messrs. Lane, Crawford, Ltd.

label: text
text: Again, the presence of a tiger on the higher levels of the Peak was reported by a very well-known resident once when he was lying off the foot of Mt. Kellet in his yacht. About the same time "pugs" of a tiger or cheetah were reported in a garden in that locality and the explanation put forward was that the animal had swum across from the mainland at some particularly narrow spot. An explanation of its presence on the mainland is not difficult to give for there is jungle harbouring many such animals between here and Canton.

label: text
text: "From an official source the 'China Mail' learns that what actually happened was that, the skin was sent Home to be stuffed, the object being to have it placed in the museum here. On its way out in stuffed form on a Japanese boat it was torpedoed, and although all the passengers were saved no-one seems to have remembered or cared enough about the tiger to rescue it from a watery grave."

label: text
text: Responsible people out in the Territories pooh-pooh the rumours of the ferocious animal which is supposed to have eaten a wood-chopper in a glen near Taipo and to resemble a cow, a kangaroo, a bear and a mammoth porcupine.

CHINESE LAW POINT.
HOW MUCH LONGER.
(From Our Own Correspondent.)
Canton, May 7

label: text
text: Evidence as to the legal rights of a fourth wife under Chinese law was given by the fourth wife of a deceased Hongkong tailor in the Supreme Court this morning. The woman claims that to her care were handed two infant sons and that she is the fit and proper person to administer the estate.

label: text
text: It is the claim of a brother of the deceased that the fourth wife had no claim to administer the estate, even though the other wives were dead and that her application for letters of administration should not be granted. As the next of kin of mature age he claims that he is the natural guardian of the boys and the most fitting person to administer the estate.

label: text
text: The stepmother of the mother of the two sons in question gave evidence this morning. They said that the fourth wife had only acted as cook during the life time of the boys' mother and that it was impossible for the latter to have handed over the care of her sons to such a person (this being one of the claims of the fourth wife in asking for letters of administration).

label: text
text: Expert evidence was also called this morning according to which under Chinese law if the fourth wife could establish her claim to be the "compassionate" mother she would be entitled to administer the estate.

label: text
text: The amount involved is $189,000. Mr. C. G. Alabaster, K.C., with Mr. Eisley Zeitlyn (instructed by Mr. J. A. Gordon Leask) was for the plaintiff (brother of deceased) and Mr. Eldon Potter, K.C., with Mr. P. C. Jenkin (instructed by Mr. H. K. Woo) defended the fourth wife.

There is an under-current of feeling that the present strained situation cannot last much longer. It is becoming increasingly apparent that Dr. Sun's followers, in spite of their announcement of a Commission (including the non-Cantonese generals) of Government to carry on in Dr. Sun's place, are merely being tolerated by the autocratic mercenary chieftains who have seized most of the important sources of revenue and are still, extending their influence as witness their action in usurping the control of the Canton Arsenal.

label: text
text: Peking is said to be aware of, and in secret accord with, the recent trend of developments. Yang Hsi-man is believed to be in league with Tuchun Tang Chi-yao of Yunnan although he has issued a denial.

label: text
text: A report that I heard today from a very well-informed source is that Yang is willing, should matters come to a head, to accept Tang's nominal superiority, and to work with Chan. However, it is doubted if Chan will be welcomed back to Cantons although he may regain a footing in a less important part of the territory. I am also told that the aggressors intend to do nothing but by a policy of quiet aggrandisement, attempt ultimately to override the Kuomintang by taking away revenue producing posts from the civil politicians. Meanwhile, they are said to be still discussing with Peking the apportionment of posts when the intrigue results in re-union with the North.

label: paragraph_title
text: JUMP INTO WATER.

label: paragraph_title
text: THIEF FAILS TO ELUDE POLICE.

label: text
text: Hemmed in between a European police officer and an Indian constable at the extreme ends of No. 5 wharf at Kowloon, a Chinese jumped into the water where he was ultimately fished out by the Indian.

label: text
text: This morning he was charged at the Marine Court with being a “reputed thief.” It seems that he is accused of having snatched a a fountain-peno from another Chinese. On cries of “gnatcher” being raised, the European chased him from the shore. end of the wharf and the Indian closed in from the outer end.

label: text
text: As no complainant was forthcoming, the charge was framed as stated. His excuse to the Magistrate (Lieut.-Com. G. F. Hole, R.N.) was that he had an altercation with a sampan owner about a fare and was pushed into the harbour.

label: text
text: A previous conviction for stealing was proved against him and he was sentenced to a month's hard labour without the option of a fine.

label: text
text: Inspector Bond of the Water Police prosecuted.
